speaker: Doctor
text: Hello, I am Dr. Agent. Please tell me, which specific antibiotic were you taking when these symptoms of low-grade fever, itchy rash, and joint pain started?

speaker: Patient
text: 8-year-old girl. The patient was brought to the emergency department because of a 2-day history of low-grade fever, itchy rash, and generalized joint pain. The rash initially started in the antecubital and popliteal fossae before spreading to the trunk and distal extremities. One week ago, she was diagnosed with acute sinusitis and started on amoxicillin. She has no history of adverse drug reactions, and her immunizations are up to date.

speaker: Doctor
text:
DIAGNOSIS READY: Amoxicillin-induced serum sickness-like reaction.

The rash starting in the flexural areas (antecubital and popliteal fossae) and spreading to the trunk and extremities, combined with fever and joint pain one week after initiating amoxicillin for sinusitis, is highly characteristic of this hypersensitivity reaction. Given the strong clinical presentation, are there any other specific symptoms like facial swelling or respiratory difficulty you are noticing?
